title: Profit-maximizing stop-loss / trailing-floor calibration for N=20: can loosening the trailing floor and/or adjusting the stop-loss beat the current win-rate-tuned baseline on per-trade profit?

tables.name: Stop-loss/trailing-floor configs vs live baseline, ranked for profit (336 tested)

notes: Direct fork of stop_trigger_swing_calibration_n20.py with the selection objective changed from win_rate+avg_pct to avg_pct alone (the direct profit proxy), and the grid widened toward looser trailing floors (trigger up to 4%, floor fraction down to 15%) and a wider stop-loss range (-1.5% to -5%). Triggered by a real finding in live trade_log.json history: 68.6% win rate since the 09-11 reset but avg_win (+0.43%) dwarfed by avg_loss (-2.53%), a ~6:1 payoff ratio needing an 85.6% win rate to break even.

conclusion.summary: 0/336 configs beat the current -3%/+0.5% baseline on avg_pct on both splits, even with the objective changed to pure profit-maximization and the grid widened toward looser trailing floors and both tighter/wider stop-losses -- the current settings remain the best of everything tested for the N=20 pool.
